summary: Phase 2.5 per-exam model routing + 5 quick-start presets. Backend 13/14 pytest pass: exam_type persists & echoes back on POST + GET-single for all 6 codes (incl. case-insensitive 'jee_mains' → JEE_MAINS upper-cased). Seeded JEE_MAINS exam (d684ab45) generated a 3-q MCQ paper in <90s, reached generation_status=ready, exam_type=JEE_MAINS stamped on paper doc, rag_anchors_used + rag_difficulty_distribution populated, MCQ structure valid. Backend log confirms primary 'LLM success with openai/gpt-5.1' (the JEE_MAINS chain head). Regression green: admin/overview, /api/textbooks, /api/papers, /api/student/textbooks all 200. Frontend E2E: /competitive-exams shows quick-create-grid with all 5 preset-* buttons; new-exam-type <select> exposes the exact 6 options ['GENERIC','JEE_MAINS','JEE_ADV','CAT','UPSC','NEET']; clicking preset-NEET created a NEET library; list shows exam-type-NEET (×2) + exam-type-JEE_MAINS (×3) badges; detail-exam-type-JEE_MAINS and detail-exam-type-NEET render on respective detail pages.

minor.issue: Legacy exam docs created before Phase 2.5 (e.g. id 422ed801-c1d5-49d1-a7fd-5aac27b9b5cd) have no `exam_type` field in MongoDB, so the list endpoint returns rows WITHOUT that key. Spec says they should default to GENERIC. Fix: either (a) one-shot migration `db.competitive_exams.update_many({'exam_type':{'$exists':False}},{'$set':{'exam_type':'GENERIC'}})` in startup, or (b) normalise on read in list_exams/get_exam (`row.setdefault('exam_type','GENERIC')`). Frontend tolerates missing key (badge only renders when set & != GENERIC), but the API contract is technically violated.

action_items: MINOR: default missing exam_type to 'GENERIC' on read in list_exams (and get_exam) OR run a one-shot migration. Pick whichever — frontend already tolerates, but API contract says default should be GENERIC.
critical_code_review_comments: Per-exam routing implementation is clean: chain_for_exam() with .upper() lookup + safe PROVIDER_CHAIN fallback; competitive_system_for_exam() correctly layers the overlay on top of COMPETITIVE_QGEN_SYSTEM. _generate_competitive_paper() reads exam.exam_type ONCE up-front and passes both system + provider_chain into chat_complete — no double-fetch. Good.

JEE_ADV / UPSC / CAT / NEET primary models (o3-pro, claude-opus-4-6, gemini-3.1-pro-preview, claude-sonnet-4-5) were NOT live-tested end-to-end this run because each takes 30-90s of LLM time and a single JEE_MAINS run was sufficient to prove the routing dispatch logic works. Per playbook, fallback chains acceptable if primary 502/rate-limits — but for an end-to-end smoke on each, recommend a separate slow-suite the main agent can opt into.

PRESETS const in CompetitiveExams.jsx is the single source of truth for the 5 preset codes — drift risk if backend EXAM_PROVIDER_CHAINS or _EXAM_SYSTEM_OVERLAYS keys evolve. Consider exposing GET /api/competitive-exams/preset-codes that returns the supported list, and have the frontend render from that response.
Minor: PRESETS in CompetitiveExams.jsx pins year (2026) in the name. Will need a yearly bump.
INFO: legacy docs missing exam_type is the only behavioural gap from the spec — see action_item above.

rca_of_the_issue: The one failing test (test_list_contains_exam_type_field) is NOT a regression of new code — it surfaces that ExamCreate added the field on writes but list_exams projects Mongo docs raw, so any legacy exam pre-Phase-2.5 returns without the key. Two-line fix: either migrate once or `for r in rows: r.setdefault('exam_type','GENERIC')` before return.
